v.note: Riya on camera, talking to the viewer

scenes.say: When I was one month old, I lost about 90 to 95% of my hearing. I’ve worn hearing aids ever since. They made accessibility a lot easier, but they don’t solve every problem.

lines: When I was one month old, I lost
about 90 to 95% of my hearing.
I’ve worn hearing aids ever since.
They made accessibility a lot easier,
but they don’t solve every problem.

scenes.say: One problem is that you can’t hear some frequencies of sound, like consonants. That makes it hard to tell these sounds apart: s, f, th, sh, ch, k, p and h.

lines: One problem is that you can’t hear some
frequencies of sound, like consonants.
That makes it hard to tell these sounds
apart: s, f, th, sh, ch, k, p and h.

scenes.say: So when you’re a kid and you can’t hear them, it’s hard to learn how to pronounce words. For the longest time, I said “chair” as “shair”, because I couldn’t hear the difference.

lines: So when you’re a kid and
you can’t hear them, it’s
hard to learn how to pronounce words.
For the longest time, I
said “chair” as “shair”,
because I couldn’t hear the difference.

scenes.say: It took a lot of speech therapy. Trying to say what you literally can’t hear is frustrating and time-consuming for the child, the parent and the therapist.

lines: It took a lot of speech therapy.
Trying to say what you literally
can’t hear is frustrating and
time-consuming for the child,
the parent and the therapist.

v.statSub: children worldwide live with deafness or disabling hearing loss

scenes.say: It’s like doing maths with your dad at the dinner table, but ten times worse. I wouldn’t wish it on my worst enemy. I’m traumatised to this day, and I’m not the only one.

lines: It’s like doing maths with your dad at

scenes.say: Here’s the problem we’re solving. Research shows that children with hearing loss are slowest to learn sounds like S and SH, because hearing aids can’t fully carry them. They’re asked to say sounds they can’t hear, with no way to check themselves.

lines: Here’s the problem we’re solving.

like S and SH, because hearing
aids can’t fully carry them.
They’re asked to say sounds they can’t
hear, with no way to check themselves.

v.sideSub: See what your voice looks like

scenes.say: So we came up with a way to visualise your voice. Soundbook is a gamified storytelling app for deaf and hard of hearing children, where they can see what their voice sounds like.

lines: So we came up with a way
to visualise your voice.
Soundbook is a gamified storytelling
app for deaf and hard of hearing
children, where they can see
what their voice sounds like.

scenes.say: The parent or therapist picks the family of sounds they want their child to practise. Each family of sounds is linked to a story.

lines: The parent or therapist
picks the family of sounds
they want their child to practise.
Each family of sounds

scenes.say: They pick a story and read it aloud with their child. Throughout the story, the child is asked to make letter sounds, like this.

scenes.say: Sssssss… I need practice, y’all. I can’t do it at my grown age.

scenes.say: The slider shows the child how soft or sharp their voice is, which is very different from quiet and loud. They can see the difference between two sounds, and get better with practice.

v.sideSub: SHH → Shell Beach · SSS → Sunflower Hill

scenes.say: The child’s voice moves the plot forward. Here, Sid and his friend need to pick where to go. The child can make either sound to choose. I choose Shell Beach, so I say “Shhh”… and there I go.

v.note: Riya on camera, personal and warm

scenes.say: Speech therapy changed my life. Now my friends understand me the first time, and I don’t think twice before raising my hand in class. But that took years. Soundbook doesn’t replace speech therapy or human support. It makes the practice in between easier and more fun, so the next kid can get there faster.

scenes.say: Claude generated a lot of options quickly, like particle stars, glowing orbs, glass sliders, and dark and light themes. We asked ourselves whether each would actually work for a five-year-old with a cochlear implant.

v.la: Before: star target over the slider
v.lb: After: a slider between two sounds

scenes.say: The particle star was beautiful, but children couldn’t tell which way to change their sound. Telling the two sounds apart was the core problem, so we moved to a simple slider between the two sounds.

lines: The particle star was
beautiful, but children couldn’t
tell which way to change their sound.
Telling the two sounds apart
was the core problem, so we
moved to a simple slider
between the two sounds.

scenes.say: The glass knob looked really nice, but a high-contrast ring works better to show children where their sound sits between the two sides.

scenes.say: Dark mode looked polished, but light mode felt more familiar, more like a storybook for children.
